answer: Horizon-sealed admission slots. Each epoch, agents derive a public seed via a delay cipher that no party can run ahead of; slot assignments are then fixed by hashing identities against that unrevealed seed. An attacker cannot precompute which identities will collide with a reef of honest slots, so mass-registering cheap identities yields low hit probability. Each wasted registration still pays full slot price, and the attacker must maintain every failed identity through the epoch to learn the outcome.
